findings.title: The 3.2a commit can't pass: tests that still expect the removed sections are only deleted later
findings.description:
Tasks 3.1 and 3.2 stop rendering the `Comprehension:` line and the `### Adoption Facts` section. The resolver still supplies both, and some tests still check that they render. Task 3.2a then requires `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core test` to pass before committing. It will fail:
- `packages/core/tests/pipeline-integration.test.ts:184` expects `Comprehension: ${COMPREHENSION}`. That case is in the probe block, which isn't deleted until 3.3.
- `packages/core/tests/adoption/adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts:102` expects `### Adoption Facts` (`FACTS_HEADING`). That file isn't deleted until 4.1.
- `packages/mcp-server/tests/integration/adoptionParity.test.ts:116` expects `Comprehension:`. The 3.2a check doesn't run MCP tests, but this commit would still break the MCP suite. The file isn't deleted until 3.6.

Either fix works:
- Drop 3.2a and commit 3.1–3.6 together at 3.7.
- Or move the deletion of those three test cases into 3.1/3.2. This is the less useful option, because that test coverage then disappears before the resolver code it covers.

findings.title: Commit points are checkbox items, not plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description:
Commit points must be plain `**Commit**:` lines, never checkboxes. Here they are checkbox tasks or sub-items:
- 2.3 (`- [ ] **2.3 Commit**`) and 3.2a are whole checkbox tasks.
- 3.7, 4.1–4.4, 5.1 and 6.3 put `- [ ] Commit: …` sub-items inside their tasks.

Convert each one to a plain `**Commit**: <message>` line after its task. Task 3.2a's success check (typecheck plus tests) can move into 3.2. As checkboxes they also push towards a commit that only checks boxes, which the project's commit rules forbid.

findings.title: The four commits in section 4 could be fewer
findings.description: Tasks 4.1–4.4 are each small deletions that commit separately. Together with the other commits, that's nine for a slice rated effort 2/5. Each one does leave the workspace compiling, so this is acceptable. Merging 4.2 and 4.3 into a single commit, "trim kept adoption modules", would cut one without losing a working state.

findings.title: 4.1 checks only core, though it deletes exports from the package index
findings.description: Task 4.1 removes re-exports from `core/src/adoption/index.ts` but only runs `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core typecheck`. Tasks 4.2–4.4 use the workspace-wide `pnpm typecheck`. Section 3 should already have removed CLI and MCP use of these exports, so the risk is low. Using `pnpm typecheck` in 4.1 would make it consistent.
